# Cadence UI — full context

# Cadence UI

> Animation-first React components for shadcn. Base UI + Tailwind CSS v4 + Motion.
> Install with `npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/<id>`. Every component ships its motion contract and a reduced-motion branch.

## Install

```json
{ "registries": { "@cadence": "https://cadence.dev/r/{name}.json" } }
```

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

## Rules for agents

- Prefer an existing Cadence component over writing new animation code.
- Read the item's `docs` and `meta.motion` before changing motion.
- Keep the reduced-motion branch; never remove `data-motion`.
- Use presets from `components/cadence/lib/motion.ts`; do not invent durations.
- Cadence is UI only: never pass a schema, resolver, or validation rule to a component (P11).

## Components

- [Button](/r/button.md): Triggers an action, with press feedback that collapses under reduced motion. (form, feedback)
- [Badge](/r/badge.md): A compact status label that stays still while the content around it animates. (feedback)
- [Kbd](/r/kbd.md): A keyboard key or shortcut hint, styled from the semantic tokens. (utility)
- [Separator](/r/separator.md): A one-pixel rule that divides groups of content. (layout)
- [Label](/r/label.md): An accessible name for a form control, with no state of its own. (form)
- [Input](/r/input.md): A single-line text field whose invalid state is driven by aria-invalid. (form)
- [Textarea](/r/textarea.md): A multi-line text field that grows with its content instead of a script. (form)
- [Card](/r/card.md): A bounded surface for grouped content, with parts you can restyle. (layout)
- [Aspect Ratio](/r/aspect-ratio.md): Reserves a box at a fixed ratio so media cannot shift the layout. (layout)
- [Avatar](/r/avatar.md): A profile image with a text fallback, a presence dot, and a stack of peers. (data)
- [Skeleton](/r/skeleton.md): A placeholder pulse that marks where content will land. (feedback, data)
- [Alert](/r/alert.md): A message about the current state of the page, with an icon column and an action slot. (feedback)
- [Empty](/r/empty.md): The resting state of a region that has nothing to show yet. (feedback, layout)
- [Item](/r/item.md): A row in a list of like objects, with media, content, and actions. (data, layout)
- [Dialog](/r/dialog.md): A modal window that fades and settles in, with the open and close sequence interruptible. (overlay)

## Docs

- [/r/registry.json](/r/registry.json): install index
- [/r/catalog.json](/r/catalog.json): machine-readable catalog
- [/llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt): every component doc inline


---

# Button

Triggers an action, with press feedback that collapses under reduced motion.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";

export function Save() {
  return <Button onClick={save}>Save changes</Button>;
}
```

## Variants

`variant` sets the visual weight. There are six, and the default one is the primary action of
the surface it sits on; reach for a different weight only when the hierarchy asks for it.

| Variant | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | The one primary action on the surface. |
| `secondary` | A supporting action next to the primary one. |
| `outline` | A neutral action that should not compete for attention. |
| `ghost` | Toolbar and icon-row actions, where the surface carries the shape. |
| `destructive` | An action that removes or overwrites data. |
| `link` | An in-flow action that reads as text. |

```tsx
<Button>Save changes</Button>
<Button variant="secondary">Preview</Button>
<Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
<Button variant="ghost">Skip</Button>
<Button variant="destructive">Delete project</Button>
<Button variant="link">Read the changelog</Button>
```

## Sizes

`size` sets the height and padding. Four text sizes cover dense toolbars through page-level
calls to action; four square sizes cover icon-only buttons.

| Size | Height | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xs` | 24px | Dense toolbars and table rows. |
| `sm` | 32px | Secondary actions in compact layouts. |
| `default` | 36px | Most buttons. |
| `lg` | 40px | Page-level calls to action. |
| `icon-xs` | 24px | Icon only, dense. |
| `icon-sm` | 32px | Icon only, compact. |
| `icon` | 36px | Icon only, default. |
| `icon-lg` | 40px | Icon only, prominent. |

```tsx
<Button size="xs">Extra small</Button>
<Button size="sm">Small</Button>
<Button size="default">Default</Button>
<Button size="lg">Large</Button>

<Button size="icon-xs" variant="ghost" aria-label="More">
  <MoreHorizontal />
</Button>
<Button size="icon-sm" variant="outline" aria-label="Search">
  <Search />
</Button>
<Button size="icon" variant="outline" aria-label="Add item">
  <Plus />
</Button>
<Button size="icon-lg" aria-label="Open settings">
  <Settings />
</Button>
```

Icon-only buttons always need an `aria-label`: the glyph is not a name.

## When to use

- The primary action of a form, dialog, or toolbar.
- A single, clearly labelled command: save, delete, invite.
- Anywhere the user expects a physical press response.

## When not to use

- Navigation between routes; use a link styled with `buttonVariants`.
- Toggling a persistent state; use `toggle` or `switch`.
- Submitting a long-running job that needs its own progress surface; pair the button with a
  spinner and a `disabled` state, or use `toast` for the result.

## Links

For navigation, keep the link and take the styles: this preserves link semantics and
middle-click.

```tsx
import Link from "next/link";
import { buttonVariants } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";

<Link href="/pricing" className={buttonVariants({ variant: "outline" })}>
  Pricing
</Link>;
```

## Composition

`render` replaces the underlying element; use it for custom button components, not for links.

```tsx
<Button render={<CopyButton />}>Copy</Button>
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "destructive" \| "outline" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "link"` | `"default"` | Visual weight. |
| `size` | `"default" \| "xs" \| "sm" \| "lg" \| "icon" \| "icon-xs" \| "icon-sm" \| "icon-lg"` | `"default"` | Height and padding. |
| `render` | `ReactElement \| (props, state) => ReactElement` | – | Base UI composition; replaces `asChild`. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. |

All native button props are forwarded.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| press | `scale 1 → 0.98` while active | `spring.press` | yes (pointer up) |
| release | `scale 0.98 → 1` | `spring.press` | yes |
| reduced | no scale; colour and shadow only | – | – |
| none | no scale; colour and shadow only | – | – |

## Accessibility

- Renders a real `<button>` through Base UI, so Enter and Space activate it natively.
- Focus is visible through the ring tokens; disabled buttons are not focusable and keep
  `aria-disabled` semantics from Base UI.
- `aria-invalid` drives the destructive border and ring. The component does not validate
  anything: see [validation](/docs/validation).

## Notes for AI

- Keep the label specific ("Delete project", not "OK").
- Do not add a `loading` boolean that hides the label; pass `disabled` and render a spinner
  next to the text so the action stays readable.

# Badge

A compact status label that stays still while the content around it animates.

## When to use

- A short status: `Active`, `Beta`, `Deprecated`, `3 open`.
- A category or tag next to a title, where the colour carries the grouping.
- A count attached to a navigation item or a filter chip.

## When not to use

- Anything the user must click to act; use `button` (a badge has no focus, no
  press feedback, and no keyboard path).
- More than about three words. A long label belongs in running text or in a `card`
  header, not in a pill.
- A status that changes while the user watches; use `toast` or an inline message,
  because a badge swap is easy to miss.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/badge
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge/badge";

export function Release() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
      <span className="font-medium">Parity plan</span>
      <Badge variant="secondary">0.2.0</Badge>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Variants

```tsx
<Badge>Default</Badge>
<Badge variant="secondary">Secondary</Badge>
<Badge variant="outline">Outline</Badge>
<Badge variant="ghost">Ghost</Badge>
<Badge variant="destructive">Failed</Badge>
<Badge variant="link">Changelog</Badge>
```

### With an icon

```tsx
import { Check } from "lucide-react";

<Badge variant="outline">
  <Check />
  Verified
</Badge>;
```

### As a link

`render` replaces the element, so a badge stays a `span` unless you ask for
something else. The `[a&]` selectors only switch on hover when it really is a link.

```tsx
<Badge variant="outline" render={<a href="/releases" />}>
  3 releases
</Badge>
```

## API

| Prop        | Type                                                                                             | Default     | Description                                      |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `variant`   | `"default" \| "secondary" \| "outline" \| "ghost" \| "destructive" \| "link"`                     | `"default"` | Visual weight.                                   |
| `render`    | `ReactElement \| (props, state) => ReactElement`                                                  | –           | Base UI composition; replaces `asChild`.         |
| `className` | `string`                                                                                          | –           | Merged last.                                     |

`data-slot="badge"` and `data-variant` are rendered from the component's state, so
you can restyle per variant from CSS without touching this file. All native span
props are forwarded.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A badge labels content; it does not enter, leave, or move.

| Phase   | Properties                          | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ----------------------------------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none                                | –     | –             |
| reduced | none                                | –     | –             |
| none    | none                                | –     | –             |

`transition-[color,box-shadow]` is state feedback on the design tokens (hover on a
linked badge, the focus ring), not motion: it never moves the box and never runs
on mount.

## Accessibility

- The badge is a `span`, so it is not in the tab order and has no role — the text
  itself is the message.
- Colour is never the only signal: every variant still carries readable text.
- When rendered as a link it inherits the anchor's semantics, focus ring, and
  keyboard behaviour, and gains `[a&]:hover` styles automatically.

## Notes for AI

- Never attach `onClick` to a badge; switch to `button` with `size="sm"`.
- Do not animate a badge in or out. If the status changes, swap the text and let
  `aria-live` on the surrounding region announce it.

# Kbd

A keyboard key or shortcut hint, styled from the semantic tokens.

## When to use

- A shortcut hinted next to a command: search, save, new item.
- A key the user should press in a flow: `Tab`, `Esc`, `↑ ↓`.
- Inside a `tooltip` or a `dropdown-menu` item, where space is short.

## When not to use

- A key that is part of running text. Write it in prose; a pill interrupts the
  sentence.
- A button that runs a command. A `kbd` is a label, not a control — it has no
  keyboard path and no press state.
- Long sequences of more than three keys. Put the shortcut in a table instead.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/kbd
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/cadence/kbd/kbd";

export function ShortcutHint() {
  return (
    <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
      Search <KbdGroup><Kbd>⌘</Kbd><Kbd>K</Kbd></KbdGroup>
    </span>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Single key

```tsx
<Kbd>Esc</Kbd>
```

### A combination

`KbdGroup` renders the keys with one gap between them and keeps the sequence
together for screen readers.

```tsx
<KbdGroup>
  <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>
  <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>
  <Kbd>P</Kbd>
</KbdGroup>
```

### Inside a tooltip

A `Kbd` inside `data-slot="tooltip-content"` inverts its colours automatically, so
the hint stays legible on the tooltip surface.

```tsx
<TooltipContent>
  Save <Kbd>⌘S</Kbd>
</TooltipContent>
```

## API

| Part       | Props                        | Notes                                            |
| ---------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `Kbd`      | native `kbd` props           | One key. `data-slot="kbd"`.                      |
| `KbdGroup` | native `kbd` props           | Wraps several keys with `data-slot="kbd-group"`. |

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A key hint is a label; it must not pulse or slide while the user
is reading it.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- Renders a real `<kbd>` element, which assistive technology reports as keyboard
  input — the same information a sighted user reads from the key shape.
- The shortcut is text, so it survives every reduced-motion mode and every colour
  theme.
- If a hint is icon-only, put the key name in `aria-label` on the `Kbd`.
- Do not attach `tabIndex`; a shortcut hint is not focusable.

## Notes for AI

- Use the platform's own glyphs (`⌘`, `⇧`, `↵`) rather than words, and keep one
  `Kbd` per physical key.
- If the shortcut is a live command, render a `button` and put the `Kbd` inside it.

# Separator

A one-pixel rule that divides groups of content.

## When to use

- Between groups inside a menu, a card footer, or a settings list.
- Between a toolbar and its content, horizontally or vertically.
- Inside a stack of sections that would otherwise merge visually.

## When not to use

- To create space. Use padding or `gap`; a rule is a boundary, not a spacer.
- Between every list item. Repetition turns a boundary into noise — grouped
  spacing does the same job with less ink.
- As a decorative flourish in a hero. That is a background, not a separator.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/separator
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Separator } from "@/components/cadence/separator/separator";

export function Account() {
  return (
    <div className="space-y-4">
      <p className="text-sm">Signed in as ada@example.com</p>
      <Separator />
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Billing is handled by finance.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Vertical

A vertical rule needs a height from its container. `self-stretch` in a flex row
gives it one for free.

```tsx
<div className="flex h-6 items-center gap-3">
  <span className="text-sm">Draft</span>
  <Separator orientation="vertical" />
  <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Edited 2 minutes ago</span>
</div>
```

### Decorative

Upstream's Base UI separator is always announced. Mark a purely visual rule as
decorative so screen readers skip it:

```tsx
<Separator decorative />
```

## API

| Prop          | Type                         | Default          | Description                                                   |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"`   | Direction of the rule.                                        |
| `decorative`  | `boolean`                    | `false`          | Renders `role="none"` and `aria-hidden`; additive to upstream. |
| `render`      | Base UI render prop          | –                | Composition, as on every Base UI primitive.                   |
| `className`   | `string`                     | –                | Merged last.                                                  |

`data-slot="separator"` and `data-orientation` are always set, so a consumer can
size the rule from CSS: `data-[orientation=vertical]:h-8`.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A boundary that animates draws the eye to the wrong thing; if the
layout changes, the surrounding `accordion` or `collapsible` owns that animation.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, which is the
  correct semantic for a group boundary.
- `decorative` removes it from the accessibility tree for rules that carry no
  meaning (a divider inside a visual layout).
- Focusable separators are not supported on purpose: a rule is not a control.

## Notes for AI

- Prefer `gap` and `space-y` first; add a separator only when two groups need a
  visible boundary.
- Never place a separator between two items of the same list. Group the list
  instead.

# Label

An accessible name for a form control, with no state of its own.

## When to use

- Every input, textarea, select, checkbox, radio, switch, and slider that needs a
  visible name.
- A group of controls that share one caption.
- A field whose purpose is not obvious from the placeholder alone (which is
  almost every field).

## When not to use

- As a placeholder. A placeholder disappears on the first keystroke and is not a
  name; use a real `Label`.
- As a heading. If the text introduces a section, use a heading so it appears in
  the document outline.
- For helper text or error text; those belong in the description/error slot so
  they can be wired through `aria-describedby`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/label
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label/label";

export function EmailField() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
      <Input id="email" type="email" autoComplete="email" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Wrapping instead of `htmlFor`

Either association works: `htmlFor` + `id`, or wrapping the control. Pick one per
field and keep it consistent.

```tsx
<Label>
  <input type="checkbox" />
  Email me about releases
</Label>
```

### Disabled

The label follows the control without any prop: `peer-disabled:` handles a sibling
control, `group-data-[disabled=true]:` handles a disabled `Field`.

```tsx
<Label htmlFor="slug" className="peer-disabled:opacity-50">
  Slug
</Label>
<Input id="slug" className="peer" disabled defaultValue="cadence" />
```

## API

| Prop        | Type              | Default | Description                          |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `htmlFor`   | `string`          | –       | Id of the control this label names.  |
| `className` | `string`          | –       | Merged last.                         |

All native `label` props are forwarded.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A label is text; the only thing it reacts to is the disabled state,
which is an opacity change on a token, not an animation.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- Renders a native `<label>`; clicking it focuses the control with no JavaScript.
- The accessible name comes from the label's text, so never hide it with
  `display: none`. If the design needs a hidden label, use `sr-only`, not removal.
- `htmlFor` must point at an `id` that exists in the same document. Duplicate ids
  break the association silently.

## Notes for AI

- One label per control. Do not add `aria-label` on the control as well; two names
  fight, and the visible one wins in some browsers and loses in others.
- Keep the label short and noun-shaped ("Email", "Workspace name"), and put the
  explanation in the description slot.

# Input

A single-line text field whose invalid state is driven by aria-invalid.

## When to use

- A single line of text the user types: email, name, slug, search, URL.
- A field that needs a native input type (`email`, `password`, `tel`, `number`,
  `file`) and therefore native mobile keyboards.
- Anywhere the browser's autofill, password manager, or form submission should
  work without a wrapper.

## When not to use

- Multi-line text; use `textarea`.
- A choice from a fixed list; use `select` (or `combobox` when the list is long).
- A value the app controls entirely, like a generated id. Render text, not a
  disabled input.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/input
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label/label";

export function WorkspaceName() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="workspace">Workspace name</Label>
      <Input id="workspace" placeholder="Acme" autoComplete="organization" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Invalid

`aria-invalid` is the only switch. The component renders the destructive border and
ring; it never decides that the value is wrong.

```tsx
<Input aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="email-error" defaultValue="ada@" />
<p id="email-error" className="text-sm text-destructive">
  Enter a complete email address.
</p>
```

### File input

`file:` variants are already wired, so the native picker button picks up the
tokens:

```tsx
<Input type="file" accept="image/png" />
```

### Controlled, Base UI style

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("");

<Input value={value} onValueChange={setValue} />;
```

## API

| Prop            | Type                                | Default | Description                                        |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`          | `string`                            | –       | Native input type.                                 |
| `value`         | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | –   | Controlled value.                                  |
| `defaultValue`  | same as `value`                     | –       | Uncontrolled initial value.                        |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string, details) => void`  | –       | Base UI change callback, in addition to `onChange`. |
| `className`     | `string`                            | –       | Merged last.                                       |

All native input props are forwarded, including `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`,
and `aria-*`.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). An input that grows, slides, or fades while the user types is a
bug: it moves the caret under the user's eyes.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

`transition-[color,box-shadow]` exists for the focus ring and the invalid border.
Both are colour/shadow state feedback on the design tokens, take no space, and do
not run on mount.

## Validation and data ownership

P11 draws the line: the component renders state, the user decides state.

| The component does                                    | You do                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Styles `aria-invalid="true"` and `data-invalid`        | Deciding what "valid" means (required, format, length)    |
| Renders whatever `aria-describedby` points at          | Writing the error text and the ids it lives on            |
| Forwards `required`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, `name`    | Form state (react-hook-form, TanStack Form, server state)  |
| Keeps focus visible and keyboard-reachable             | Submit, retry, error mapping, focus management             |

There is no `schema`, `resolver`, `validate`, or `rules` prop, and no validation
library is imported. See [validation](/docs/validation).

## Accessibility

- Base UI's input is field-aware: inside a `field`, it receives the label id and
  the description ids without extra wiring.
- Always give it a name from a `label`; a placeholder is not a name.
- `aria-invalid` plus a described error is the accessible failure state. Colour
  alone is never the signal.
- Never set `outline: none` in `className`; the focus ring is the only affordance
  for keyboard users.

## Notes for AI

- Use `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` — never an `error` prop or internal
  state.
- Do not wrap the input in a div just to add a border; the component already owns
  the border, radius, and focus ring.

# Textarea

A multi-line text field that grows with its content instead of a script.

## When to use

- A sentence or a paragraph: a comment, a description, a commit message, a note.
- A field where the user's text is longer than the visible box should be.
- Anywhere the browser's native resize handle is useful.

## When not to use

- A single line (email, name, slug); use `input`.
- Rich text. A `textarea` holds plain text; formatting needs an editor, which is
  out of scope for this library.
- A value that must stay fixed in height; a `textarea` grows, and a fixed box hides
  the overflow from the user.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/textarea
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label/label";
import { Textarea } from "@/components/cadence/textarea/textarea";

export function Comment() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="comment">Comment</Label>
      <Textarea id="comment" rows={4} placeholder="Leave a note for the reviewer" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Auto-growing

`field-sizing-content` lets the browser grow the box as the text gets longer. No
JavaScript, no `ResizeObserver`, no layout read during render.

```tsx
<Textarea className="min-h-16 max-h-48" placeholder="Type and watch the box grow" />
```

### Resizable by the user

```tsx
<Textarea className="resize-y" rows={3} />
```

### Invalid

```tsx
<Textarea aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="bio-error" />
<p id="bio-error" className="text-sm text-destructive">
  Keep it under 280 characters.
</p>
```

## API

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description               |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------- |
| `className` | `string` | –       | Merged last.              |

All native `textarea` props are forwarded, including `rows`, `maxLength`,
`required`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, and `aria-*`.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). Growth is the browser sizing the box, not an animation: on a
`field-sizing-content` textarea the height changes with the text as you type, and
a transition on it would lag behind the caret.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Validation and data ownership

Same contract as `input`: the field renders state, you own the state.

| The component does                                 | You do                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Styles `aria-invalid="true"`                       | Deciding validity (length, format, required)             |
| Renders what `aria-describedby` points at           | Writing the error text and the counter ("12 / 280")      |
| Forwards `required`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, `name` | Form state and submission                                |

Character counters are yours to render: the component does not count. Keep the
count in the description slot and point `aria-describedby` at it, so a screen
reader hears it before the limit is hit.

## Accessibility

- Renders a native `<textarea>`, so Enter inserts a newline and Escape does not
  close anything — expected behaviour in a form.
- Give it a `label`, and never rely on the placeholder as a name.
- If you cap the length with `maxLength`, say so in the description; a silent stop
  in typing reads as a broken field.
- `resize-y` keeps the horizontal layout stable; full `resize` lets a long word
  break the page.

## Notes for AI

- Do not implement auto-resize with a `scrollHeight` loop; `field-sizing-content`
  is the CSS-only answer and it matches upstream.
- Never own the character count in component state. Render it next to the field and
  wire it through `aria-describedby`.

# Card

A bounded surface for grouped content, with parts you can restyle.

## When to use

- A unit of content that belongs together: a summary, a plan, an account, a
  record in a grid.
- A surface that needs a header, an optional action, body content, and a footer.
- A list of comparable items where the boundary itself carries meaning.

## When not to use

- To fake spacing. A card is a boundary; use padding if you only need breathing
  room.
- As a page layout. Nesting cards inside cards flattens the hierarchy.
- For a modal or a popover; those are overlays with their own focus rules.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/card
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Card,
  CardContent,
  CardDescription,
  CardFooter,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/card/card";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";

export function Plan() {
  return (
    <Card className="max-w-sm">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Parity plan</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>57 components, nine batches, one release train.</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Batch B1 ships the eleven atoms.</p>
      </CardContent>
      <CardFooter>
        <Button variant="outline">Open plan</Button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Action in the header

`CardHeader` switches to two columns when a `CardAction` is present — no extra
prop, no manual grid.

```tsx
<CardHeader>
  <CardTitle>Members</CardTitle>
  <CardDescription>12 people have access.</CardDescription>
  <CardAction>
    <Button size="sm" variant="outline">Invite</Button>
  </CardAction>
</CardHeader>
```

### Compact

`size="sm"` tightens every part at once, because the spacing lives in one custom
property on the root:

```tsx
<Card size="sm">…</Card>
```

### Section boundaries

Add a rule with utilities rather than a new part; the `[.border-b]` selectors are
already wired:

```tsx
<CardHeader className="border-b">…</CardHeader>
<CardFooter className="border-t">…</CardFooter>
```

## API

| Part              | Props                     | Notes                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Card`            | `size`, native div props  | `size`: `"default" \| "sm"`. Sets `--card-spacing` and `data-size`. |
| `CardHeader`      | native div props          | Grid header; reacts to `CardAction` and a bottom border.  |
| `CardTitle`       | native div props          | Bold, leading-none. Does not create a heading.            |
| `CardDescription` | native div props          | Muted supporting text.                                    |
| `CardAction`      | native div props          | Top-right slot inside the header.                         |
| `CardContent`     | native div props          | Body; carries the horizontal padding.                     |
| `CardFooter`      | native div props          | Bottom row; reacts to a top border.                       |

Every part sets `data-slot`, so CSS can reach it:
`[&>[data-slot=card-header]]:gap-4`.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A card does not fade, lift, or scale in. If a group of cards should
appear in sequence, that is a page-level `list.stagger` decision made by the parent,
not a property of the card.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- `Card` is a plain `div`: no role, no landmark. That is correct for a visual
  grouping — but it means the card is not a navigable region. If a set of cards is
  the main content, wrap it in a `<section>` or a list (`<ul>/<li>`).
- `CardTitle` renders a `div`. When the title belongs in the document outline, put
  a heading inside it: `<CardTitle><h3 …>Parity plan</h3></CardTitle>`, or render
  the card with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title's id.
- A card that is clickable must contain a real link or button; do not put
  `onClick` on the card and call it done — it is invisible to keyboard users.

## Notes for AI

- Use `CardFooter` for actions, not a bare `div` — it keeps spacing consistent when
  `size` changes.
- Do not add hover lift to a card that is not interactive. Motion on a static card
  is decoration (P9).

# Aspect Ratio

Reserves a box at a fixed ratio so media cannot shift the layout.

## When to use

- An image, video, or embed whose intrinsic size is unknown until it loads.
- A thumbnail grid that must not reflow as the images arrive.
- A placeholder that will be replaced by media of a known shape.

## When not to use

- Fixed-size icons or avatars; give them a size and be done.
- Text blocks. A ratio box around text clips exactly the content that needs to grow.
- A container whose height should follow its content — that is a normal block.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/aspect-ratio
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/cadence/aspect-ratio/aspect-ratio";

export function Cover() {
  return (
    <AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9} className="overflow-hidden rounded-lg">
      <img src="/cover.jpg" alt="Dashboard preview" className="size-full object-cover" />
    </AspectRatio>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Square

```tsx
<AspectRatio ratio={1} className="overflow-hidden rounded-full">
  <img src="/avatar.jpg" alt="" className="size-full object-cover" />
</AspectRatio>
```

### Video

```tsx
<AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9}>
  <iframe
    src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/…"
    title="Walkthrough"
    className="size-full"
    allowFullScreen
  />
</AspectRatio>
```

### Multiple ratios in one grid

Each box keeps its own ratio, so the grid stays stable while media loads:

```tsx
<div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-4">
  <AspectRatio ratio={4 / 3} className="overflow-hidden rounded-md"><img … /></AspectRatio>
  <AspectRatio ratio={4 / 3} className="overflow-hidden rounded-md"><img … /></AspectRatio>
  <AspectRatio ratio={4 / 3} className="overflow-hidden rounded-md"><img … /></AspectRatio>
</div>
```

## API

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                                            |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ratio`     | `number` | –       | Width ÷ height. Required — there is no sensible default. |
| `className` | `string` | –       | Merged last; `overflow-hidden` and the radius go here.  |

The ratio is written as `--ratio`, and the box uses `aspect-(--ratio)`. Your own
`style` is preserved: the custom property is merged after it.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). The whole point of the box is that it does not change size; a
transition here would reintroduce the layout shift it exists to prevent.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- The box is a layout element with no role. Put the meaning on the media: a real
  `alt` on images, a `title` on iframes.
- A background-only ratio box (no media yet) is decorative — keep it empty, or give
  it `aria-hidden` if it would otherwise be an empty accessible node.
- Media that animates (autoplay video, GIF) counts against both the CLS budget and
  the reduced-motion contract; pause or replace it under
  `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Notes for AI

- Always pass a `ratio`; `16 / 9` for video, `1` for avatars, `4 / 3` for photos.
- Put `object-cover` on the child, not on the ratio box. The box only reserves
  space; the child fills it.

# Avatar

A profile image with a text fallback, a presence dot, and a stack of peers.

## When to use

- A person or an entity next to content they own: a comment, an assignee, a commit.
- A stack of participants, with a `+3` tile for the rest.
- A presence indicator on a collaborator, via `AvatarBadge`.

## When not to use

- A logo that must stay legible at small sizes; use the image with a fixed box.
- A decorative illustration; avatars imply a person or an account.
- More than about five faces. Past that the stack stops being readable — use
  `AvatarGroupCount` with a name list in the tooltip.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/avatar
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarFallback, AvatarImage } from "@/components/cadence/avatar/avatar";

export function Author() {
  return (
    <Avatar>
      <AvatarImage src="/ada.png" alt="Ada Lovelace" />
      <AvatarFallback>AL</AvatarFallback>
    </Avatar>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Sizes

`size` sets `data-size` on the root; every child reads it through `group/avatar`.

```tsx
<Avatar size="sm">…</Avatar>
<Avatar>…</Avatar>
<Avatar size="lg">…</Avatar>
```

### Presence

```tsx
<Avatar>
  <AvatarImage src="/ada.png" alt="Ada Lovelace" />
  <AvatarFallback>AL</AvatarFallback>
  <AvatarBadge className="bg-emerald-600" />
</Avatar>
```

### Group

```tsx
<AvatarGroup>
  <Avatar><AvatarImage src="/ada.png" alt="Ada Lovelace" /><AvatarFallback>AL</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
  <Avatar><AvatarFallback>GH</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
  <AvatarGroupCount>+3</AvatarGroupCount>
</AvatarGroup>
```

## API

| Part               | Props                        | Notes                                                        |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Avatar`           | `size`, Base UI root props   | `size`: `"default" \| "sm" \| "lg"`. Sets `data-size`.        |
| `AvatarImage`      | Base UI image props          | `src`, `alt`. Hidden automatically when the image fails.      |
| `AvatarFallback`   | Base UI fallback props       | Rendered while loading and after an error.                    |
| `AvatarBadge`      | native span props            | Corner dot; sized from the root's `data-size`.                |
| `AvatarGroup`      | native div props             | Overlapping stack with a ring in the page colour.             |
| `AvatarGroupCount` | native div props             | The `+3` tile that closes a stack.                            |

All parts carry `data-slot`, so `[&>[data-slot=avatar]]:size-6` style overrides are
possible without a prop.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). The image-to-fallback swap is instant by design: Base UI knows when
the image errored, and a cross-fade would show a half-drawn face in the meantime.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- `AvatarImage` is an `<img>`: always pass a real `alt`. With a name beside the
  avatar, use `alt=""` so it is not announced twice.
- `AvatarFallback` prints initials. Those initials are the accessible name when the
  image is missing, so derive them from the person's actual name.
- `AvatarBadge` is a visual dot. Give it a text alternative when the presence state
  matters — e.g. `<span className="sr-only">Online</span>` inside it, or an
  `aria-label` on the badge.
- An avatar that links to a profile must be wrapped in an `<a>` with an accessible
  name; the image `alt` alone is not a link name.

## Notes for AI

- Always render an `AvatarFallback`; without it a failed image leaves an empty hole.
- Do not animate the presence dot. State lives in the DOM (`aria-label`, text), not
  in a pulse.

# Skeleton

A placeholder pulse that marks where content will land.

## When to use

- A first load longer than about 300 ms, where the shape of the incoming content is
  known: a card, a table row, a list item, a comment.
- A region that swaps content in place, so the layout does not jump when the real
  content arrives.
- A page that renders several independent regions which resolve at different times.

## When not to use

- A wait under 300 ms. The placeholder appears and disappears before it can be
  read, which reads as a flicker.
- An action the user just triggered (a save, a submit); use the button's own busy
  state or a `spinner`, so the feedback lands where the user is looking.
- Content whose shape you do not know. A placeholder that is the wrong shape is
  worse than a spinner: it promises a layout that never arrives.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/skeleton
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@/components/cadence/skeleton/skeleton";

export function CardPlaceholder() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-sm space-y-3" aria-busy="true" aria-live="polite">
      <Skeleton className="h-40 w-full rounded-xl" />
      <Skeleton className="h-4 w-2/3" />
      <Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/2" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Text lines

```tsx
<div className="space-y-2">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-11/12" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-3/5" />
</div>
```

### Avatar and name

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-3">
  <Skeleton className="size-10 rounded-full" />
  <div className="space-y-2">
    <Skeleton className="h-3 w-32" />
    <Skeleton className="h-3 w-20" />
  </div>
</div>
```

### Swapping in the real content

Keep the container mounted so the height is continuous; only the children change.

```tsx
<section aria-busy={loading}>
  {loading ? <CardPlaceholder /> : <Card>…</Card>}
</section>
```

## API

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                                        |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `className` | `string` | –       | Merged last — the shape (`h-4 w-2/3`) lives here.   |

All native `div` props are forwarded. `data-slot="skeleton"` and `data-motion` are
always set.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `data.transition`, a continuous opacity loop. It is implemented in CSS
(`animate-pulse`) rather than in Motion, because a page can render dozens of
placeholders and each Motion loop costs a frame callback; the pulse only touches
`opacity`, so it can never trigger layout.

| Phase   | Properties                | Token                          | Interruptible |
| ------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------- |
| pulse   | `opacity 1 → 0.5 → 1`     | `animate-pulse` (theme timing) | yes (CSS)     |
| reduced | same pulse, opacity only  | `animate-pulse`                | yes (CSS)     |
| none    | no animation; full opacity | `animate-none`                 | –             |

Reduced keeps the pulse on purpose: M5 removes travel and scale, not opacity, and a
static grey block is easier to mistake for content that already loaded. `none`
stops it completely, which is what a screenshot test or a print stylesheet needs.

## Keyboard interactions

None. A skeleton is not focusable and never receives input; focus stays on whatever
the user was doing when the region started loading.

## Accessibility

- The skeleton itself is decorative: its text is nothing, so it is not announced.
- The **region** owns the state: `aria-busy="true"` while loading, removed when done.
  Add `aria-live="polite"` there only if the region resolves without any other
  change the user would notice.
- Shape is a promise. Keep the placeholder's height close to the real content, or
  the swap reintroduces exactly the layout shift the skeleton was meant to avoid.
- Under `data-motion="none"` the block stays visible at full opacity: the loading
  state is still communicated by shape and by `aria-busy`, never by motion alone.

## Responsive behavior

A skeleton takes its size from utilities, so it follows whatever grid it is dropped
into. Avoid a hard-coded pixel height on a full-width block; use a ratio
(`aspect-video`) or a relative height so the placeholder matches the real card at
every breakpoint.

## Performance

- One CSS animation per element, on `opacity` only; no JS loop, no layout read.
- The pulse is compositor-friendly, but the animation-system budget still applies:
  fewer than twenty simultaneously animating elements. For a long list, render one
  placeholder row per screen rather than one per future row.
- No `will-change`: the browser promotes an opacity animation on its own.

## Notes for AI

- Never animate a skeleton into the real content with a custom cross-fade; swap the
  children and let the container's height stay put.
- Put the loading state on the region (`aria-busy`), not on each block.
- Do not use a skeleton as a generic "loading…" indicator for an action; a `spinner`
  next to the control is clearer.

# Alert

A message about the current state of the page, with an icon column and an action slot.

## When to use

- The result of an action the user just took, where the outcome needs a sentence of
  explanation: a failed deploy, a partial import, a quota that is nearly full.
- A state of the page that is not an error but changes what is possible — degraded
  mode, read-only mode, a plan that expired yesterday.
- A warning attached to a region rather than to a control, so it survives scrolling
  away from the field it is about.

## When not to use

- A confirmation that needs no reading ("Saved"). Use `toast`: an alert stays in the
  layout, and stale success messages become noise.
- A decision that blocks progress. That is `alert-dialog`, which traps focus on
  purpose.
- Ordinary guidance or onboarding copy. An `alert` is a live region; using it for
  static text makes screen readers interrupt the user for nothing.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/alert
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { CircleAlert } from "lucide-react";
import { Alert, AlertDescription, AlertTitle } from "@/components/cadence/alert/alert";

export function QuotaNotice() {
  return (
    <Alert>
      <CircleAlert />
      <AlertTitle>You are close to the build limit</AlertTitle>
      <AlertDescription>12 of 15 builds used this month.</AlertDescription>
    </Alert>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### With an action

`AlertAction` spans both grid rows, so it stays on the first line when the
description wraps.

```tsx
<Alert variant="destructive">
  <TriangleAlert />
  <AlertTitle>Deploy failed</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>Build 42 exited with code 1.</AlertDescription>
  <AlertAction>
    <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Retry</Button>
  </AlertAction>
</Alert>
```

### Without an icon

The icon column collapses to zero, so title and description sit flush left. Add an
icon only when it tells the user something the title does not.

```tsx
<Alert>
  <AlertTitle>Read-only mode</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>Billing needs attention before you can edit.</AlertDescription>
</Alert>
```

### Destructive

`variant="destructive"` colours the text and leaves the surface as a card. A red
block is harder to read and competes with the page it sits on.

```tsx
<Alert variant="destructive">Payment declined</Alert>
```

## API

| Part               | Props                    | Notes                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Alert`            | `variant`, native props  | `variant`: `"default" \| "destructive"`. Always `role="alert"`. |
| `AlertTitle`       | native div props         | One line, medium weight, second grid column.                    |
| `AlertDescription` | native div props         | Muted text; paragraphs inside keep relaxed leading.             |
| `AlertAction`      | native div props         | Right-aligned slot, spans both rows.                            |

Every part sets `data-slot` (`alert`, `alert-title`, `alert-description`,
`alert-action`), so a consumer can restyle without new props:
`[&>[data-slot=alert-title]]:text-base`.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). An alert that slides or fades in draws attention to the animation
instead of the message, and a message that is already on screen when the page loads
did not change — animating it is decoration (P9).

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

The border and text colours are state feedback on the design tokens; they are not
animated and carry no timing.

## Accessibility

- `role="alert"` makes the alert an assertive live region. Mount it when the state
  appears; do not keep a permanent alert in the tree and toggle its text, because
  every change interrupts whatever the screen reader was saying.
- The icon is decorative — mark it `aria-hidden` if it duplicates the title. An
  icon inside a link or a button is different: that one needs its own name.
- `variant="destructive"` is colour plus a title that says what happened. Never rely
  on the colour alone: the message has to be readable in greyscale.
- The action is a real control. If it is the only way forward, it must be reachable
  by keyboard and come after the message in DOM order (it does).

## Notes for AI

- Use an alert for a state that persists; use `toast` for a moment.
- Keep exactly one `role="alert"` per message. Nesting parts does not add roles —
  only `Alert` sets one.
- Do not pass an `onClose` and hide it with opacity; that is a toast, not an alert.

# Empty

The resting state of a region that has nothing to show yet.

## When to use

- A list, table, or panel that is legitimately empty: no invoices, no results for
  this filter, a folder nobody has filled yet.
- An empty state that teaches the next step — a primary action, a link to a
  template, or a line that explains what will appear here.
- A region whose emptiness is a state, not a mistake: an inbox at zero, a fresh
  workspace.

## When not to use

- While loading. Use `skeleton` when the shape of the incoming content is known,
  and `spinner` when it is not.
- A search that returned nothing because of a typo. That case needs the query echoed
  back and the filter explained, not a generic illustration.
- An error. An empty region is a normal state; a failed request is an `alert`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/empty
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Inbox } from "lucide-react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";
import {
  Empty,
  EmptyContent,
  EmptyDescription,
  EmptyHeader,
  EmptyMedia,
  EmptyTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/empty/empty";

export function InvoicesEmpty() {
  return (
    <Empty>
      <EmptyHeader>
        <EmptyMedia variant="icon">
          <Inbox />
        </EmptyMedia>
        <EmptyTitle>No invoices yet</EmptyTitle>
        <EmptyDescription>Invoices you send will land here.</EmptyDescription>
      </EmptyHeader>
      <EmptyContent>
        <Button size="sm">Create invoice</Button>
      </EmptyContent>
    </Empty>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Bounded or unbounded

The root is a dashed container with generous padding, so it can stand in for a whole
panel. Drop the boundary with a class when it already sits inside a bordered card.

```tsx
<Empty className="border">…</Empty>
```

### A second action

`EmptyContent` is a column with a gap; put the secondary action underneath, or side
by side with a row wrapper.

```tsx
<EmptyContent>
  <Button size="sm">Import CSV</Button>
  <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">Start from a template</Button>
</EmptyContent>
```

### Icon or illustration

`variant="icon"` puts the glyph on a muted surface; `default` leaves the media
transparent for an illustration or a small chart.

```tsx
<EmptyMedia variant="icon">
  <Inbox />
</EmptyMedia>
```

## API

| Part               | Props                   | Notes                                                          |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Empty`            | native div props        | Centred flex column, dashed boundary, `md:p-12`.               |
| `EmptyHeader`      | native div props        | Stacks media, title, description; `max-w-sm`.                  |
| `EmptyTitle`       | native div props        | Large, medium weight. Renders a `div`, not a heading.          |
| `EmptyDescription` | native props for `p`    | Renders a `div` (upstream too): the copy often holds a block.  |
| `EmptyMedia`       | `variant`               | `"default" \| "icon"`, exposed as `data-variant`.              |
| `EmptyContent`     | native div props        | Actions; full width, `max-w-sm`, own gap.                      |

`data-slot` values are `empty`, `empty-header`, `empty-title`,
`empty-description`, `empty-icon`, `empty-content`.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). An empty state is a resting state: it is what the region looks like
when nothing is happening. Fading it in would make it look like content arriving,
which is the one thing it is not.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

When the region swaps from empty to populated, that transition belongs to the list
(`list.stagger` or `data.transition`), not to this component.

## Accessibility

- The root is a plain container: no role, no live region. Announce the change of
  state in the region that owns it (`aria-live="polite"` on the list), not here.
- `EmptyTitle` renders a `div`. If the empty state is the main content of a page,
  put a real heading inside it so it appears in the outline.
- The media is decorative. Pass `aria-hidden` to the icon, or give the surrounding
  text the whole message — an icon alone never carries meaning.
- Keep at least one action focusable. An empty state with no way forward is a dead
  end; the primary action is the reason this component exists.

## Notes for AI

- One primary action per empty state. Two competing buttons read as a decision the
  user is not ready to make.
- Do not build an empty state out of `Card` plus padding; the boundary, the rhythm,
  and the description width are already decided here.
- Do not use `Empty` for a loading placeholder — `skeleton` keeps the layout stable,
  which `Empty` does not.

# Item

A row in a list of like objects, with media, content, and actions.

## When to use

- A list of comparable objects where each row carries a name, a line of supporting
  text, and an action: files, members, invoices, saved searches.
- A row that must become a link as a whole, without nesting a button inside an
  anchor.
- A dense list where three sizes (`default`, `sm`, `xs`) cover a panel, a card, and a
  sidebar strip respectively.

## When not to use

- Tabular data with columns that need to line up across rows. Use `table`: an item is
  a sentence, not a grid.
- A single object on its own page. Use `card`; the item's rhythm assumes siblings.
- A selectable row inside a menu or a listbox. Those have their own roles and
  keyboard model; use the menu or `command` component.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/item
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { FileText } from "lucide-react";
import {
  Item,
  ItemContent,
  ItemDescription,
  ItemGroup,
  ItemMedia,
  ItemTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/item/item";

export function Files() {
  return (
    <ItemGroup>
      <Item>
        <ItemMedia variant="icon">
          <FileText />
        </ItemMedia>
        <ItemContent>
          <ItemTitle>parity-plan.md</ItemTitle>
          <ItemDescription>Edited 4 minutes ago by you.</ItemDescription>
        </ItemContent>
      </Item>
    </ItemGroup>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### A whole-row link

`render` replaces the wrapper element (Base UI `render`, not `asChild`). The anchor
keeps `data-slot="item"`, so CSS and `group/item` selectors still work.

```tsx
<Item render={<a href="/files/plan" />}>
  <ItemContent>
    <ItemTitle>plan.pdf</ItemTitle>
    <ItemDescription>2.4 MB</ItemDescription>
  </ItemContent>
</Item>
```

### Variants

`default` is transparent, `outline` adds the border, `muted` fills the surface. The
border is always present in the box model — only its colour changes — so switching
variants never shifts the layout.

```tsx
<Item variant="outline" />
<Item variant="muted" size="sm" />
```

### Separators

`ItemSeparator` is a horizontal `Separator` with the vertical margins removed, so it
sits flush between rows.

```tsx
<ItemGroup>
  <Item>…</Item>
  <ItemSeparator />
  <Item>…</Item>
</ItemGroup>
```

### Header and footer

`ItemHeader` and `ItemFooter` take a full row (`basis-full`), for metadata above the
title or a progress line below the content.

```tsx
<Item>
  <ItemHeader>
    <ItemTitle>Quarterly report</ItemTitle>
    <Badge variant="outline">Draft</Badge>
  </ItemHeader>
  <ItemFooter>
    <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Updated 2h ago</span>
  </ItemFooter>
</Item>
```

## API

| Part              | Props                                  | Notes                                                           |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Item`            | `variant`, `size`, `render`            | `variant`: `default \| outline \| muted`; `size`: `default \| sm \| xs`. |
| `ItemGroup`       | native div props                       | `role="list"`; wraps rows and separators.                       |
| `ItemMedia`       | `variant`                              | `default \| icon \| image`, exposed as `data-variant`.          |
| `ItemContent`     | native div props                       | Grows; a second content block stops growing.                    |
| `ItemTitle`       | native div props                       | One line, medium weight.                                        |
| `ItemDescription` | native props for `p`                   | Clamped to two lines, muted.                                    |
| `ItemActions`     | native div props                       | Right-aligned controls.                                         |
| `ItemHeader`      | native div props                       | Full-width row above the content.                               |
| `ItemFooter`      | native div props                       | Full-width row below the content.                               |
| `ItemSeparator`   | `Separator` props                      | Horizontal rule with `my-0`.                                    |

`Item` writes `data-slot="item"`, `data-variant`, and `data-size`; the other parts
write their own `data-slot` (`item-media`, `item-content`, `item-title`,
`item-description`, `item-actions`, `item-header`, `item-footer`,
`item-separator`).

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A row does not lift on hover or slide on mount. The only transition
is `transition-colors` on the row and on a link inside it — state feedback that
costs nothing and never moves the text the user is reading.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

If a list should arrive in sequence, that is `list.stagger` on the parent. A row
that animates itself cannot be interrupted by the next render.

## Accessibility

- `ItemGroup` sets `role="list"`. Rows are `div`s (or an anchor via `render`), so
  give the group a label when it is not already under a heading:
  `aria-label="Files"`.
- A row that links nowhere is a container. If the whole row is clickable, render an
  anchor with `render` rather than adding `onClick` — the anchor is focusable,
  middle-clickable, and announced as a link.
- `ItemMedia variant="icon"` is decorative in most rows; add `aria-label` to the
  icon only when it carries information the title does not.
- Keep action buttons out of the tab order of a read-only list. Put them in
  `ItemActions` and reveal them on hover **and** focus, never hover alone.

## Notes for AI

- Reach for `Item` when the row is a sentence about one object; reach for `table`
  when the columns are the point.
- `size="sm"` and `xs` do not change type: they change padding and gaps. Use them for
  density, not hierarchy.
- Use `ItemSeparator`, not `border-b` on the row: the separator keeps the variant
  border colour independent of the divider.

# Dialog

A modal window that fades and settles in, with the open and close sequence interruptible.

## When to use

- A focused task that must interrupt the page: rename, invite, confirm.
- Content that needs a modal, a focus trap, and an obvious escape route.
- A short form whose result matters more than the page behind it.

## When not to use

- Non-blocking hints and menus; use `popover` or `tooltip`.
- Long multi-step flows; use a page or a wizard.
- Mobile sheets with drag gestures; use `drawer`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/dialog
```

This also installs `button`, which the dialog uses for its close control.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dialog/dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";

export function DeleteProject() {
  return (
    <Dialog>
      <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Delete project</DialogTrigger>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Delete this project?</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>This removes every deployment and cannot be undone.</DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <DialogFooter>
          <DialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
          <Button variant="destructive">Delete project</Button>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <DialogContent>…</DialogContent>
</Dialog>;
```

### Without the built-in close button

```tsx
<DialogContent showCloseButton={false}>…</DialogContent>
```

### Footer with a close action

```tsx
<DialogFooter showCloseButton>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</DialogFooter>
```

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI root. |
| `DialogTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the dialog. |
| `DialogContent` | `showCloseButton`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. |
| `DialogOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `DialogContent`. |
| `DialogClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the dialog. |
| `DialogHeader` / `DialogFooter` | `className` | Layout only. |
| `DialogTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `DialogDescription` | `className` | Optional supporting text. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | overlay `opacity 0 → 1`; panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.95 → 1` | `popup.anchored` | yes |
| exit | overlay `opacity → 0`; panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.95` | `exit.fade` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, 100ms | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | instant | – | – |

The panel stays mounted while its exit transition runs; Base UI delays unmount until the
transition ends, so reopening mid-exit reverses cleanly.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the dialog. |
| Escape | Closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. |

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`,
  focus trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling.
- The close button is a real button with a screen-reader-only label.
- `DialogTitle` is required; a dialog without an accessible name is invalid.
- Content is unmounted after the exit transition, so focus is never lost mid-flight.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is centred and capped at `max-w-lg`; on narrow viewports it keeps a 1rem gutter.
Long content scrolls inside the popup rather than the page.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open.
- Animates opacity and scale only; no layout reads and no JavaScript animation loop.

## Notes for AI

- Always render a `DialogTitle`; it is the accessible name.
- Keep the confirming action specific ("Delete project", not "OK").
- Do not animate height inside the dialog; mount content instead.
